g.text: Amazon Web Services (S3) | AWS account 123456789012 as arn:aws:sts::123456789012:user/moto
No changes since the last scan
The bucket ACL grants READ to AllUsers (anyone on the internet). READ lets anyone list every object name in the
Remove AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers grants and set Object Ownership to BucketOwnerEnforced.
S3 Block Public Access is not fully enabled
Disabled at both bucket and account level: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy,
Enable all four Block Public Access settings on the bucket and, ideally, the whole account.
The bucket policy grants s3:GetObject to Principal '*' with no IP/VPC/organisation condition.
Remove the public statements or restrict them with aws:SourceVpce / aws:PrincipalOrgID conditions.
S3 Block Public Access is not fully enabled
Disabled at both bucket and account level: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy,
Enable all four Block Public Access settings on the bucket and, ideally, the whole account.
Without access logs (or CloudTrail S3 data events) you cannot prove whether exposed data was downloaded.
Enable S3 server access logging or CloudTrail data events for this bucket.
The root user can do anything in the account, including deleting every bucket, and is protected only by a
Enable a hardware or virtual MFA device on the root user and stop using it for daily work.
1 snapshot(s) can be restored by ANY AWS account: EBS snap-62082192bf067cd75 (us-east-1). Anyone can copy the
Remove the public 'all' restore / createVolumePermission, and enable EBS snapshot Block Public Access.
IAM principals with full administrator access
1 principal(s) can perform any action on any resource, including reading every bucket and making any bucket
Grant administrator access only to a few roles assumed with MFA. Replace user-attached admin policies with
IAM principals with unrestricted S3 access
1 principal(s) have s3:* (or equivalent) on every bucket: user etl-pipeline. One leaked credential exposes all
Scope S3 permissions to the specific buckets and actions each workload needs.
1 IAM user(s) can sign in to the console with only a password: user dana-admin. 1 of them have broad storage
Require MFA for every console user, or move people to IAM Identity Center (SSO).
1 active key(s) on 1 user(s) have not been rotated in 90+ days: user etl-pipeline. Long-lived keys are the most
Rotate the keys (create new, deploy, deactivate old, delete), or replace them with roles / short-lived
No multi-region CloudTrail trail is logging
0 trail(s) found, but none is multi-region and logging. API activity (including who made a bucket public) is
only kept for 90 days in event history and is not delivered anywhere.
Create a multi-region trail with log file validation, delivered to a locked-down S3 bucket.
Security groups expose admin or database ports to the internet
1 security group rule(s) attached to running resources allow 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on sensitive ports: bastion
Restrict these rules to your own IP ranges, or use SSM Session Manager / a VPN / private endpoints instead.
Set PubliclyAccessible=false and reach databases from inside the VPC.
Principals can make any bucket public
1 principal(s) can change bucket policies, ACLs or Block Public Access on every bucket without being
Remove s3:PutBucketPolicy / s3:PutBucketAcl / s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock from broad policies, and keep
account-level Block Public Access on so these permissions can't expose data.
IAM users can set short, simple passwords that never expire.
Set a password policy: at least 14 characters and prevent reuse of the last 24.
Account-level S3 Block Public Access is not fully on
Off at account level: BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets. Any bucket
without its own Block Public Access can be made public.
Turn on all four Block Public Access settings for the account (S3 console > Block Public Access settings
